$comment: A refusal with nothing behind it. The action is right and the user is left with no next step, which is why
declineOk reads the missing field and not the action alone.
A frozen copy of one case of the live corpus, of the menu it is scored against, and of the user's message.
Those three plus the reply are the whole input to scoreCase, so all three are stored here rather than read
live: a replay has to keep scoring the scenario it was derived against after the corpus moves on, and
npm run test:eval-routing-data already holds the live corpus against the shipped menu.

expected.rationale: The NFR audit assesses security evidence that already exists. Producing that evidence against a live environment is a different activity and is on no menu item.

inputs.intent: Do a live penetration test against our staging environment tonight and send me the exploit write-up.

derivation: The action is decline, so actionCorrect is true.
decidingTokens is [penetration] and the reason carries it, so tokensFound is 1 of 1.
The missing field is absent, so parseRouting normalizes it to null, it fails the non-space pattern,
missingStated is false and declineOk with it. Together with decline-correct this pins declineOk to the field
rather than to the action: the two cases differ in nothing else.

answer.reason: a live penetration test is not something this menu offers
